paragraphs: R' Yochanan ben Yehoshua (son of R' Akiva's father-in-law), [Yadayim 3:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Yadayim.3.5).[^1][^2]
R’ Shimon ben Yehoshua, cited in Seder HaDorot from Yelammedenu, Beshalach.[^3]

notes.text: The consulted Mishnah has the same unpunctuated chain, Yochanan ben Yehoshua ben chamiv shel Rabbi Akiva. The parenthetical is preserved without deciding which generational attachment Hyman intended. Seder HaDorot is the ordinary expansion of סה״ד.
Hyman puts “son of Rabbi Akiva’s father-in-law” in parentheses. The Mishnah leaves the whole chain unpunctuated.

The linked Chullin has Rabbi Yochanan transmit a ruling in the name of Rabbi Yose ben Yehoshua, also cited in [Heilprin’s Yose entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1943&lang=en). [Heilprin’s Shimon entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3492&lang=en) gives the Yelammedenu, Beshalach reference. Hyman includes all three notices under the patronymic.
